label: Sequence-start step for a fixed 18-token subset, plus first copy output step (t=4) when L=3
explanation: Two regimes. (1) At t=0, the first original token, it fires exactly when that token is in a fixed subset {a,b,d,h,i,k,m,o,p,q,s,t,u,v,x,y,1,2}. The activation there depends only on the token (a=0.18 of max, t=0.16, m=0.13, d/o=0.10, k=0.07, 2=0.06, y=0.03). It never fires at t=0 on c,e,f,g,j,l,n,r,w,z,0,3. This regime covers 96% of active steps but only 75% of activation mass. (2) In length-3 sequences it fires on the step right after <DEL> (t=4, recall_idx=1, where orig(0) is fed back as input), for every first token. These steps carry the largest activations (up to the max, often 0.9+ of max), and together they hold about 25% of the mass. On L=4 sequences the step after <DEL> fires only rarely and weakly (69 dev steps, ~0% mass). The unit is silent at all other original-phase positions, at the delimiter, and at every other copy step. Dev split: P=1.00, R=0.999.

issues: The only systematic misses are at the step right after <DEL> in L=4 sequences (t=5): 76 test steps carrying 0.1% of mass. The explanation already says so (69 dev steps).
Saying the L=3 t=4 activations are 'often above 0.9 of max' is a little generous. The top examples are 0.90-1.00, but a second-quartile example sits at 0.55.

Every other claim checked out. The t=0 term has dev precision 1.0, recall 0.957 and mass 0.751. The token indices map to {a,b,d,h,i,k,m,o,p,q,s,t,u,v,x,y,1,2}. The L=3 post-<DEL> term has precision 1.0 and fires in all 2605 L=3 sequences, carrying 0.249 of mass. Nothing fires at t=1-3, at <DEL>, or at t>=6. Test has 0 false positives.
